plan.target: Incorrect Cache-Block Management Operation Decode for cbo.inval with CBIE=01 (src/ieu/controller.sv and src/cache/cachefsm.sv)
plan.rationale:
In `src/ieu/controller.sv` lines 391-395, cache-block management operation decode assigns operation codes to `CMOpD[2:0]` with an internal semantic mismatch that causes `cbo.inval` under `CBIE == 2'b01` to execute as `cbo.clean` (clean without invalidating) rather than `cbo.flush` (clean and invalidate).

According to the RISC-V Capacity and Cache-Block Management (Zicbom) Specification (v1.0.4, Section 2, 'Cache-Block Management Instructions') and the RISC-V Privileged Architecture Specification (v20211203, Section 3.1.12, 'Machine Environment Configuration Registers'):
When `menvcfg.CBIE == 2'b01`, execution of a `cbo.inval` instruction in a less-privileged mode (e.g., S-mode or U-mode) MUST perform a flush operation, identical to `cbo.flush`. A flush operation consists of a clean operation followed by an invalidate operation: it writes back the cache block to memory if dirty, and unconditionally invalidates the cache block in all levels of the cache hierarchy (clearing the valid bit).

In `src/ieu/controller.sv` lines 391-395:
```systemverilog
    if ((P.ZICBOM_SUPPORTED) & CMOD) begin
      CMOpD[2] = (InstrD[31:20] == 12'd2); // cbo.clean
      CMOpD[1] = (InstrD[31:20] == 12'd1) | ((InstrD[31:20] == 12'd0) & (ENVCFG_CBE[1:0] == 2'b01)); // cbo.flush
      CMOpD[0] = (InstrD[31:20] == 12'd0) & (ENVCFG_CBE[1:0] == 2'b11); // cbo.inval
    end
```
In RISC-V Zicbom, `12'd2` (0x002) is actually `cbo.flush`, while `12'd1` (0x001) is `cbo.clean`. The designer swapped the semantic comments on lines 392 and 393 (`CMOpD[2]` is flush, `CMOpD[1]` is clean). Consequently, when implementing the specification rule that `CBIE == 2'b01` makes `cbo.inval` perform a flush, the designer mistakenly OR'd `((InstrD[31:20] == 12'd0) & (ENVCFG_CBE[1:0] == 2'b01))` into `CMOpD[1]` instead of `CMOpD[2]`.

In `src/cache/cachefsm.sv` lines 159-161:
```systemverilog
assign ClearValid = (CurrState == STATE_ACCESS & (CMOpM[0] | (CMOpM[2] & ~HitLineDirty))) |
                    (CurrState == STATE_WRITEBACK & CMOpM[2] & CacheBusAck);
```
In `cachefsm.sv`, cache line invalidation (`ClearValid`) is controlled strictly by `CMOpM[0]` (`cbo.inval` with `CBIE=11`) and `CMOpM[2]` (`cbo.flush`). `CMOpM[1]` (`cbo.clean`) performs writeback if dirty (`CMOWriteback`) and clears dirty (`ClearDirty`), but never asserts `ClearValid`.

Because `controller.sv` line 393 mistakenly ORs the `CBIE == 2'b01` condition into `CMOpD[1]` instead of `CMOpD[2]`, executing `cbo.inval` when `CBIE == 2'b01` asserts `CMOpM[1]` and leaves `CMOpM[2] = 0`. As a result, `ClearValid` is never asserted; the cache block is written back if dirty but remains valid (`Valid = 1`) in the D-cache. The instruction performs a clean operation instead of the architecturally mandated flush operation.

This bug has been deterministically verified in simulation using `rv64gc_testbench`: a positive control test using `cbo.flush` correctly clears the valid bit (causing a subsequent load to miss in D-cache, `hpmcounter14` diff >= 1, exiting code 0), whereas `cbo.inval` under `CBIE = 01` fails to clear the valid bit (the subsequent load hits in D-cache, `hpmcounter14` diff == 0), branching to an unhandled trap/abort that trips the testbench watchdog assertion (exit code 134).

     `CMOpD[2] = (InstrD[31:20] == 12'd2); // cbo.clean` (funct12 12'd2 is cbo.flush!)

     The author swapped the semantic naming comments of `CMOpD[1]` and `CMOpD[2]`, and mistakenly mapped the `CBIE == 2'b01` condition to `CMOpD[1]` (clean) instead of `CMOpD[2]` (flush).

   - `src/privileged/csrc.sv` lines 105, 171-177: `CounterEvent[14] = DCacheMiss`, counting data cache misses via `hpmcounter14`. Both `mcounteren` and `scounteren` must be enabled to allow S-mode access to `hpmcounter14`.

fixer.report:
Root Cause: In `src/ieu/controller.sv` lines 392-393, the RISC-V Zicbom specification mandates that when `menvcfg.CBIE == 2'b01`, execution of `cbo.inval` (funct12 = 0x000) must perform a flush operation identical to `cbo.flush` (funct12 = 0x002). However, the `CBIE == 2'b01` condition was erroneously OR'd into `CMOpD[1]` (which maps to funct12 0x001, `cbo.clean`) instead of `CMOpD[2]` (which maps to funct12 0x002, `cbo.flush`). Since `src/cache/cachefsm.sv` only asserts `ClearValid` for `CMOpM[0]` (cbo.inval with CBIE=11) and `CMOpM[2]` (cbo.flush), the `cbo.inval` with `CBIE=01` was routed through the `cbo.clean` path (`CMOpM[1]`), which performs a writeback if dirty but never invalidates the cache line (never asserts `ClearValid`).

Minimal Fix: Moved the `((InstrD[31:20] == 12'd0) & (ENVCFG_CBE[1:0] == 2'b01))` from `CMOpD[1]` to `CMOpD[2]` in `src/ieu/controller.sv`. Changed 2 lines in 1 file.

File changed: `src/ieu/controller.sv` (2 insertions, 2 deletions).

Targeted Test Outcome: The reproducer script now exits with code 0 (was exit code 134 before fix). The positive control test (`test_cbo_flush_control.elf`) passes with exit 0, and the bug reproducer test (`test_cbo_cbie.elf`) now passes with exit 0, confirming that `cbo.inval` under `CBIE=01` correctly flushes and invalidates the cache line.
